1. verus! {
2. 
3. //==================================================================================================
4. // View
5. //==================================================================================================
6. 
7. impl View for FrameNumber {
8.     type V = int;
9. 
10.     // `closed`: callers reference `self@`, but the mapping to the inner `usize` field is hidden.
11.     // The abstract value is "the frame index as int". When `arch` is verified this realizes the
12.     // kernel's uninterpreted `spec_frame_raw_value(frame)`.
13.     closed spec fn view(&self) -> int {
14.         self.0 as int
15.     }
16. }
17. 
18. //==================================================================================================
19. // Abstract bound + type invariant
20. //==================================================================================================
21. 
22. impl FrameNumber {
23.     // Models `FrameNumber::MAX = MAX_ADDRESS / FRAME_SIZE - 1`: the largest representable frame
24.     // index. A module-wide constant, not per-value state. It is `uninterp` (its concrete value
25.     // bottoms out at the build-time page-size constants, an external boundary) and is tied to the
26.     // exec constant `FrameNumber::MAX` by the `assume_specification` below. Realizes the kernel's
27.     // uninterpreted `spec_max_frame_number()` (see `hal/mem/types/address/phys.spec.rs`). The `nat`
28.     // result makes the bound non-negative for callers (e.g. constructing `FrameNumber::NULL`).
29.     pub uninterp spec fn spec_max() -> nat;
30. 
31.     // Every constructible `FrameNumber` is bounded by `MAX`. Enforced as a type invariant so the
32.     // bound holds unconditionally for any value callers hold (PTE/PDE treat it as an always-valid
33.     // token), which is exactly what lets `into_raw_value() << FRAME_SHIFT` not overflow `usize`.
34.     #[verifier::type_invariant]
35.     pub open spec fn inv(&self) -> bool {
36.         0 <= self@ <= Self::spec_max()
37.     }
38. }
39. 
40. //==================================================================================================
41. // Exec constant binding
42. //==================================================================================================
43. 
44. // Ties the exec constant `FrameNumber::MAX` to the abstract `FrameNumber::spec_max()`. `MAX`'s body
45. // (`MAX_ADDRESS / FRAME_SIZE - 1`) bottoms out at build-time page-size constants that Verus treats
46. // as external; this trusted contract names that boundary without interpreting it.
47. pub assume_specification[ FrameNumber::MAX ] -> (result: usize)
48.     ensures
49.         result as int == FrameNumber::spec_max() as int,
50. ;
51. 
52. } // verus!
53.

3. 
4. //==================================================================================================
5. // Imports
6. //==================================================================================================
7. 
8. use vstd::prelude::*;
9. #[cfg(verus_keep_ghost)]
10. include!("number.spec.rs");
11. #[cfg(verus_keep_ghost)]
12. include!("number.proof.rs");
13. 
14. use crate::mem;
15. 
16. //==================================================================================================
17. // Structures
18. //==================================================================================================
19. 
20. ///
21. /// # Description
22. ///
23. /// A type that represents a frame number.
24. /// A frame number is in the range from `0` to [`Self::MAX`] (inclusive).
25. ///
26. #[verus_verify]
27. #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy)]
28. pub struct FrameNumber(usize);
29. 
30. //==================================================================================================
31. // Implementations
32. //==================================================================================================
33. 
34. // `MAX` is kept in a plain (non-`#[verus_verify]`) impl so Verus treats it as external: its value
35. // bottoms out at the build-time page-size constants, and its abstract value is supplied by the
36. // `assume_specification[FrameNumber::MAX]` in `number.spec.rs`.
37. impl FrameNumber {
38.     /// The maximum frame number.
39.     pub const MAX: usize = mem::MAX_ADDRESS / mem::FRAME_SIZE - 1;
40. }
41. 
42. #[verus_verify]
43. impl FrameNumber {
44.     #[verus_spec(ensures Self::NULL@ == 0)]
45.     pub const NULL: Self = Self(0);
46. 
47.     ///
48.     /// # Description
49.     ///
50.     /// Constructs a [`FrameNumber`].
51.     ///
52.     /// # Parameters
53.     ///
54.     /// - `value`: The value of the frame number.
55.     ///
56.     /// # Returns
57.     ///
58.     /// - `Some(`[`FrameNumber`]`)`: Upon success.
59.     /// - `None`: If the value is greater than [`Self::MAX`].
60.     ///
61.     #[verus_spec(result =>
62.         ensures
63.             value as int <= Self::spec_max() ==> (result is Some
64.                 && (result->Some_0)@ == value as int),
65.             value as int > Self::spec_max() ==> result is None,
66.     )]
67.     pub fn from_raw_value(value: usize) -> Option<Self> {
68.         if value > Self::MAX {
69.             return None;
70.         }
71. 
72.         Some(Self(value))
73.     }
74. 
75.     ///
76.     /// # Description
77.     ///
78.     /// Converts a [`FrameNumber`] into a raw value.
79.     ///
80.     /// # Returns
81.     ///
82.     /// The raw value of the target [`FrameNumber`].
83.     ///
84.     #[verus_spec(result =>
85.         ensures
86.             result as int == self@,
87.             0 <= self@ <= Self::spec_max(),
88.     )]
89.     pub fn into_raw_value(self) -> usize {
90.         proof! { use_type_invariant(self); }
91.         self.0
92.     }
93. }
94.

96. // Unit Tests
97. //==================================================================================================
98. 
99. /// Tests if [`FrameNumber::from_raw_value()`] successfully constructs frame zero.
100. #[test]
101. fn test_frame_number_from_raw_value_zero() {
102.     let raw_value: usize = 0;
103.     let frame_number: FrameNumber = FrameNumber::from_raw_value(raw_value).unwrap();
104.     assert_eq!(frame_number.into_raw_value(), raw_value);
105. }
106. 
107. /// Tests if [`FrameNumber::from_raw_value()`] successfully constructs the maximum frame number.
108. #[test]
109. fn test_frame_number_from_raw_value_max() {
110.     let raw_value: usize = FrameNumber::MAX;
111.     let frame_number: FrameNumber = FrameNumber::from_raw_value(raw_value).unwrap();
112.     assert_eq!(frame_number.into_raw_value(), raw_value);
113. }
